correctness.rationale: For a Hermitian 3x3 K, Q_K(z)=[1,z,z^2]^*K[1,z,z^2] restricts to a real quartic on each horizontal line, whose x^4 and x^3 coefficients are identical across heights (c,2w). Four distinct zeros per line force the restrictions to be c times their corresponding monic quartics. Equality of cubic coefficients gives c*(sum r - sum s)=0. If the sums differ, c=0 and both restricted cubics vanish identically, leaving a one-dimensional real kernel spanned by H_h with determinant 2. A rank<=2 nonzero kernel is therefore impossible. If sums agree, the linear restrictions yield an independent kernel K1 with c=1; det(K1+tH_h) is an odd-degree real cubic with nonzero leading coefficient 2, hence has a real zero at a nonzero singular kernel matrix. Three distinct sample functionals span C3 by Vandermonde, excluding semidefinite nonzero kernel matrices; the singular element is indefinite rank2 and gives two genuinely distinct phaseless polynomials. Independent SymPy verification gives detH=2 and sample linear ranks 8/7 for unequal/equal centroids. The general minimality at N=8 uses Conca et al Proposition 5.4 with M=3,N<=7.
correctness.risk: Universal exact injectivity, not a uniform noise-stability estimate; h must be nonzero and each row must have four distinct nodes.
